thread:
lee (docs): Noticed a Ruby quickstart that uses ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'] in some places and ENV['API_KEY'] in others. That's causing a bunch of "401 missing auth" reports from the sample app users.

lee (docs): Example mismatch in quickstart/snippets/ruby.md: ```ruby
# BAD - inconsistent env var names
client = Redwood::Client.new(ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'])
# later in README: export API_KEY=...
```

tara (devex): Ugh. Small copy/paste error but very confusing for newbies. Also the sample-app's entrypoint retries forever on network errors without jitter. Users hit rate limits and then the app spins.

kai (sdk): I can patch the snippet to use a single canonical env var REDWOOD_API_KEY and add a short section on local dev (direnv / dotenv) + a note about not committing .env files.

kai (sdk): For retries, I'll update the sample app to use our SDK's default backoff helper instead of a naive loop. Proposed pseudo: ```ruby
# use SDK.client.with_retry(backoff: :exponential, max_attempts: 5) do |client|
#   client.generate(...)
# end
```

lee (docs): Please also update the quickstart index and the getting-started onboarding page—there's a link to the old gist. I'll add a little callout: "If you see 401, check REDWOOD_API_KEY env var name."

ci-bot: docs-lint failure -> quickstart/ruby.md: code-block contains env var name mismatches. See https://ci.internal/jobs/1138

tara (devex): Could we add a docs-check rule to grep for multiple different env var names in the same doc? Might catch these copy/paste gotchas.

kai (sdk): Good idea. I'll add a linter regex that flags more than one capitalized _KEY var in a file. Also adding tests for sample-app to assert it uses SDK retry wrapper.

lee (docs): Opening issue #1041 and will attach the PR link when ready. Thanks all — tiny fixes but huge reduction in first-run friction. :raised_hands:
